subject: Priority capacity safeguard & path to premium SLA — CardinalPay renewal
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@cardinalpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cardinalpay.com, Elena Vostrikova <elena@cardinalpay.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:14:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes today — urgent remediation request

Evelyn —

We saw two significant tail-latency incidents this morning (08:03 and 08:47 PT) that caused a non-trivial number of failed authorization flows for our card-not-present checks. Attached is a short extraction from our telemetry (latency_report_20260812.pdf) showing P95/P99 spikes and correlation with specific model routes.

This is particularly painful because our renewal window opens next month and the executive team is asking whether we can count on the current SLA. We need:

- Immediate mitigation plan (what can you do in the next 48 hrs to stop the tail spikes)
- A commitment on a path to higher availability/latency guarantees tied to our renewal (we may need premium protections)
- A draft of the credit/exception process if incidents persist

Please escalate — we depend on sub-200ms P95 for many synchronous flows and the drops this morning were visible to customers.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendez
Head of Platform
CardinalPay

Attachments: latency_report_20260812.pdf

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:01:07 -07:00

Carlos —

Really sorry you hit this. I’ve looped in our SRE and Sales lead so we can move fast. Immediate next steps (today):

1) SRE triage now — we’ll share root-cause signals within 6 hours.
2) Temporary routing to a priority capacity pool for your critical routes (we can enable this as a short-term mitigation within 12–24 hrs).
3) Ben will follow with a commercial path (pilot for priority capacity + SLA amendment draft).

I hear the renewal timing — we’ll make the commercial path explicit so your procurement and exec teams can evaluate. I’ll stay owner on the remediation and the renewal conversation.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Account Solutions | Redwood Inference
p: (415) 555-0143

Subject: Priority capacity safeguard — pilot proposal and SLA sketch

Carlos —

Thanks for raising this. We ran a quick post-mortem with infra and SRE. Short story: transient queuing on a shared GPU pool under a traffic wave amplified KV-cache churn for the route you use most. We can do three things in parallel:

A) Immediate: Enable a short-term priority pool for your critical routes (no infra change on your end) — roll takes ~12 hours and will be monitored by our SREs.
B) Pilot: 30-day dedicated "Priority Capacity Guard" pilot (reserved vGPU lanes + strict isolation for pinned model routes). SLA for pilot: 99.99% availability, P95 latency target of 220ms for the pinned routes, automated fallback to compatible model variants if a resource constraint is hit.
C) Commercial: Pricing uplift of ~28% for the dedicated pool during pilot; if you convert to an annual reserved commitment within 60 days after pilot completion we’ll credit back 50% of the pilot uplift.

Also attached is an SLA amendment draft (SLA_amendment_draft.docx) that captures the availability target, monitoring hooks, incident credit calculation, and an ops playbook. Two notes:

- We want a 90-day evaluation period in the amendment for production traffic patterns before any long-term SLA lock.
- Legal/procurement redlines are expected; we can accept standard procurement language from your PO to expedite.

If this looks sensible I can get legal to prep a DocuSign and Monica can coordinate the SRE runbook for the pilot.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_amendment_draft.docx
From: Elena Vostrikova <elena@cardinalpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cardinalpay.com, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@cardinalpay.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:02:53 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority capacity safeguard — pilot proposal and SLA sketch

Ben / Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick proposal. A few clarifying items from procurement/legal:

1) Incident credit calculation: we need a simple credit formula tied to customer-facing errors + downtime windows (not internal SRE terms). Please include an example calculation in the amendment.
2) Term: if we accept the pilot and then convert to an annual commitment we’ll need a 12-month minimum with a right-to-exit clause for the first 60 days if SLOs are not met.
3) PO timeline: our procurement ops needs ~2 weeks to route internal approvals and then a standard PO. Can you provide a DocuSign link we can review?

Also, because our platform is geo-sharded, we need assurance that the priority pool routing can be applied per-region (we operate US-West and US-East flows separately).

Elena Vostrikova
Head of Procurement, CardinalPay

Subject: Re: Priority capacity safeguard — pilot proposal and SLA sketch

Elena / team —

Operational checklist (what we’ll do during the 30-day pilot):

- Per-region routing: enable priority pool in US-West first (target date 2026-08-26), then US-East as secondary on a rolling 48-72h window.
- Monitoring hooks: we’ll expose a per-route dashboard (token-level latency histograms, tail metrics, error rates) and a webhook for incident starts/ends.
- Fallback behavior: automated model-variant fallback with a configurable percent of traffic (default 10%) to avoid total denial.
- Runbook & SRE on-call: Redwood will provide a dedicated SRE rotation for the pilot; weekly syncs with your platform team.
- Acceptance: SLO acceptance criteria defined for conversion (P95 <= 220ms and availability >= 99.99% over a 30-day window).

Procurement/Legal notes: Ben’s team can surface the draft DocuSign; we recommend the PO reference the SLA amendment ID CP-PRIO-01 so legal has a single artifact to review.

I’ll coordinate the kickoff once sign-off is received.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Next steps for Redwood: please send the DocuSign (SLA amendment + pilot terms) and the SRE kickoff calendar invite. We’ll have procurement expect a 10-business-day approval cycle.
